input.quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows far beyond the fallback ceiling of 60 days: Base Agreement § 4.0 requires six months (approx. 180 days) notice, and SOW § 2.0 requires twelve months' notice to avoid a further six-month renewal (i.e. notice must be given before the renewal even begins). Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback on a material term and binds us as customer to an unworkable exit mechanic. Redline cuts IBM's window to 30 days and normalises the SOW renewal period to 12 months, while leaving MSL's notice period untouched to protect supply continuity. Price uplift is not an issue: renewals continue "under the same terms and conditions", so no cap is needed; the absence of a vendor reminder mechanic is noted only.

proposal.summary: Cut IBM's non-renewal notice window to 30 days and set the SOW renewal term to 12 months
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened our non-renewal notice window to thirty days (our playbook allows no more than sixty) and set the renewal period to twelve months, leaving MSL's own notice period unchanged so supply continuity is preserved. As drafted, we would have to give six months' notice under the Base Agreement and twelve months' notice under the SOW to avoid a six-month auto-renewal, which is an unworkable exit.
